proof: Before slicing the value, the parser rejects a semicolon preceding the equals sign, advances equal beyond every leading ASCII space, and rejects end-of-input or equality with the semicolon boundary. Hence the value starts with at least one non-space byte before its end. Removing trailing spaces cannot remove that byte: last>=0 always. The original string_view implementation applies the same separator/leading-space/end checks before find_last_not_of. Immutable primitive strings are required; no input mutation or replaced methods are part of this domain.
scope: Only the zero-hit false alternative of the trailing-space trim guard; retain trim, all statements and functions.
upstreamNote: Redundant defensive condition under the established parse invariants; no incorrect upstream result demonstrated.
